build.why_a_new_build_was_required: Both pre-existing Spark builds (~/polygraph-server-lane/llama.cpp/build and .../build-fixed) have GGML_CUDA:BOOL=OFF in their CMakeCache.txt -- neither can exercise #26334's mechanism, which requires a CUDA device to be present in the model's `devices` list so a GPU host buffer type competes with KleidiAI's CPU extra buffer type. A new build was genuinely required; no existing artifact fit.
build.why_ggml_native_off_and_arm_arch_set: Deliberate choice, disclosed here: on this exact machine (gcc 13.3 + Cortex-X925), the DOCUMENTED KleidiAI build line (-DGGML_CPU_KLEIDIAI=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release alone, GGML_NATIVE defaulting ON) compiles ZERO kai_run_matmul symbols -- that is this project's OWN separate, already-filed finding (ggml-org/llama.cpp#26547 / Finding 3). Using that broken default here would confound #26334's buffer-ordering bug with #26547's compile-time bug and make it impossible to tell which one caused 0 dispatch hits. So this build uses the SAME GGML_NATIVE=OFF + GGML_CPU_ARM_ARCH workaround this project's own build-fixed/ already uses, confirmed below to compile real kai_run_matmul symbols, and adds GGML_CUDA=ON on top. This means the reproduction below isolates #26334's mechanism specifically -- it does NOT reproduce izard's exact reported command line/build if their gcc/CPU-table combination also had #26547's zero-symbol bug (unknown -- they disclosed no compiler or CPU model).

source_verification.no_host_flag: common/arg.cpp:2377-2380 -- `--no-host` sets params.no_host = true, which is exactly the `no_host` parameter make_cpu_buft_list() checks.
source_verification.dev_none_flag: common/arg.cpp:1077-1097 (parse_device_list) -- a single 'none' device name pushes only a null device (skips ggml_backend_load_all() and any real device), producing an effectively empty devices list for make_cpu_buft_list()'s host-buffer loop.

llama-cpp-kleidiai-cuda-ngl0-baseline.name: llama-cpp-kleidiai-cuda-ngl0-baseline
llama-cpp-kleidiai-cuda-ngl0-baseline.description: Reproduction rig for ggml-org/llama.cpp#26334: llama-cli built with -DGGML_CPU_KLEIDIAI=ON -DGGML_CUDA=ON, run with -ngl 0 (CPU-only inference) and NEITHER --no-host NOR -dev none. Not an upstream-shipped preset -- a one-off variant of tools/targets/llama-cpp-kleidiai.json with -ngl 0 appended to the workload, created only to drive this reproduction. Do not treat 'tested: false' as a defect; it means this exact JSON has not accumulated the multi-platform verified_against history the base preset has.
llama-cpp-kleidiai-cuda-ngl0-baseline.why_it_matters: Per make_cpu_buft_list() in src/llama-model.cpp, when a CUDA device is present in the model's devices list (independent of -ngl, which only zeroes compute-offloaded layers) and --no-host/-dev none are NOT passed, a GPU host (pinned-memory) buffer type is inserted into the CPU buffer-type priority list ahead of KleidiAI's extra-buft entry. select_weight_buft() then picks the first accepting buft in list order, so tensors are given the CUDA host buft before KleidiAI's extra buft is ever tried -- silently bypassing KleidiAI even though -ngl 0 was passed and the KLEIDIAI=1 banner still prints. This is the exact mechanism ggml-org/llama.cpp#26334's reporter (izard) described and gaugarg-nv (NVIDIA CUDA-backend maintainer) confirmed with a doc/policy-level reply; the issue was closed via a documented workaround, not a code fix, and nobody in the thread produced a measured before/after.

raw_llama_cli_log_excerpts.note: Captured from a plain, undecorated `llama-cli ... --verbose` invocation (same argv polygraph's L2 stage builds), grepped for the load-bearing lines. Full logs are ~1000-1500 lines each (per-tensor DEBUG lines dominate) and are not embedded in full here; the load-bearing lines are quoted verbatim below.

baseline_A.devices_still_include_cuda_despite_ngl0: llama_prepare_model_devices: using device CUDA0 (NVIDIA GB10) (000f:01:00.0) - 118862 MiB free
baseline_A.kleidiai_banner_says_on: kleidiai: primary q4 kernel feature I8MM
baseline_A.the_bug_itself: done_getting_tensors: tensor 'token_embd.weight' (q8_0) (and 290 others) cannot be used with preferred buffer type CUDA_Host, using CPU instead
baseline_A.interpretation: 291 tensors had CUDA_Host as their PREFERRED buffer type (i.e. select_weight_buft() picked the GPU host buft first, before ever reaching KleidiAI's extra buft later in the list), then fell back straight to plain 'CPU' (not to KleidiAI) because mmap forces that downgrade without re-consulting the extra-buft list. KleidiAI's own buffer type is never even named as a candidate here.

workaround_nohost_B.the_fix_visible: done_getting_tensors: tensor 'token_embd.weight' (q8_0) (and 124 others) cannot be used with preferred buffer type CPU_KLEIDIAI, using CPU instead
workaround_nohost_B.interpretation: Only 124 (not 290) tensors fall back, and this time the PREFERRED buffer type is CPU_KLEIDIAI itself -- KleidiAI's extra buft now wins the priority race and is used for the great majority of weights (322.89 MiB reported under 'CPU_KLEIDIAI model buffer size'/'common_memory_breakdown_print'). The residual fallback is KleidiAI's own known, narrower limitation (no q4_1 kernel; see 'kleidiai: no kernel for tensor type q4_1, not accelerated' -- unrelated to #26334).

workaround_devnone_D.the_fix_visible: done_getting_tensors: tensor 'token_embd.weight' (q8_0) (and 124 others) cannot be used with preferred buffer type CPU_KLEIDIAI, using CPU instead
workaround_devnone_D.interpretation: Identical outcome to --no-host (same 124-tensor residual, same CPU_KLEIDIAI preferred buft), but via a different mechanism: CUDA is excluded from the model's devices entirely (backend_ptrs.size()==1, no CUDA0 line in sched_reserve, 'CPU compute buffer size' instead of 'CUDA0 compute buffer size'), rather than merely skipping the host-buffer step while keeping CUDA available for compute scheduling.

interleaved_sweep.note: Per project hard rule 3, round-robin interleaved (order A,B,D,A,B,D,... -- see run_interleaved.py), 5 reps per arm, all three arms in the same interleave so no arm's reps are ever run consecutively/isolated from the others. This is a DISPATCH-HIT-COUNT comparison, not a wall-clock timing comparison (polygraph's L3 says nothing about performance -- see interpretation.not_established below) -- interleaving + repetition here is extra rigor to rule out a one-off fluke, not a timing requirement.

interleaved_sweep.headline: 5/5 reps: arm A (baseline, no workaround) = 0 L3 dispatch hits every time (verdict NO_DISPATCH_OBSERVED, exit 1). 5/5 reps: arm B (--no-host) = 7968 hits every time (verdict I8MM_HYBRID_DISPATCH, exit 0). 5/5 reps: arm D (-dev none) = 7968 hits every time (verdict I8MM_HYBRID_DISPATCH, exit 0). Zero spread in all three arms across 15 total runs -- fully deterministic on this workload (short prompt, 4 tokens, threads=2).

established: The mechanism ggml-org/llama.cpp#26334's reporter (izard) described, and gaugarg-nv (NVIDIA CUDA-backend maintainer) confirmed only at a doc/policy level, is REAL and REPRODUCIBLE at current HEAD (dbadb68ee, 2026-08-05): running llama-cli built with both -DGGML_CPU_KLEIDIAI=ON and -DGGML_CUDA=ON, with -ngl 0 and neither --no-host nor -dev none, silently routes weight tensors to a CUDA host buffer type first, which then downgrades to plain CPU (bypassing KleidiAI entirely) -- confirmed by real, non-halting gdb breakpoints on all 10 kai_run_matmul_* symbols recording ZERO hits, 5/5 interleaved reps, exit code 1.

Both of gaugarg-nv's documented workarounds (--no-host and -dev none) independently and completely fix it on this build: both produce 7968 real KleidiAI kernel dispatch hits (I8MM + dotprod families), 5/5 interleaved reps each, exit code 0 -- and they do so via genuinely different device-topology paths (--no-host keeps CUDA0 in the compute-scheduling graph; -dev none excludes CUDA entirely), yet land on the identical KleidiAI dispatch outcome.

The KLEIDIAI=1 startup banner and the 'kleidiai: primary q4/q8 kernel feature I8MM' selection lines print IDENTICALLY in all three arms (buggy and both fixed) -- confirming the L2 signal the issue thread said was uninformative here: banner-watching alone cannot distinguish the buggy run from either fixed run.

The one runtime diagnostic that DOES distinguish them -- 'cannot be used with preferred buffer type X, using Y instead' -- is visible in this reproduction (because --verbose raises verbosity to INT_MAX, which is >= the line's LLAMA_LOG_DEBUG gate) and names the exact buffer type: 'CUDA_Host' (291 tensors) in the buggy arm vs 'CPU_KLEIDIAI' (125 tensors, KleidiAI's own known q4_1 gap only) in both fixed arms. At llama.cpp's DEFAULT verbosity this line would not print at all, matching the issue thread's claim that a default-verbosity user gets zero indication anything was skipped.

L1 static symbol scanning is identical and unaffected across all three arms (10/149 kai_run_matmul_* symbols in libggml-cpu.so in every run) -- confirming this is purely a runtime buffer-type-selection bug, not a compile-time symbol problem (i.e., independent of and additional to this project's own already-filed #26547).
not_established: We did NOT reproduce izard's exact machine: they disclosed only 'Linux' and a version hash, no CPU model or compiler. This build deliberately used this project's own GGML_NATIVE=OFF + GGML_CPU_ARM_ARCH workaround to keep KleidiAI's symbols genuinely compiled in (ruling out this project's own #26547 zero-symbol failure mode as a confound) -- so this reproduction demonstrates the CODE MECHANISM #26334 describes, on hardware where it is buildable, not a byte-for-byte match of the reporter's environment.

No performance/timing claim is made anywhere in this file. Polygraph's L1/L2/L3 layers establish WHETHER the KleidiAI kernel executed, not by how much the fallback path is slower. Establishing that a run got 0 real KleidiAI dispatch hits (vs the reporter's qualitative '~2x slower') is a different, narrower claim than a measured throughput cost -- no interleaved timing sweep was run for this reproduction because none of the hard evidence needed to answer 'did the code path the OP diagnosed still exist' requires one.

We did not determine whether host-buffer-before-extra-bufts ordering in make_cpu_buft_list() is an intentional design trade-off (favoring GPU-offload compatibility for weight-buffer prefetch) or an unprioritized bug. This file shows the observable runtime consequence of the current ordering; it does not, and cannot, adjudicate upstream's design intent.

The reporter's specific proposed code fix (reordering extra-bufts ahead of the host buft) was never evaluated here -- this reproduction ran ONLY the current HEAD behavior plus the two already-documented CLI workarounds, not any patched build.

ggml-org/llama.cpp#26334 is closed via a user-confirmed workaround, not a merged code change. The honest framing supported by this evidence is: 'the mechanism the OP diagnosed still appears present at HEAD (verified against dbadb68ee, 2026-08-05) even though the issue is closed as resolved-by-workaround' -- not that the issue was never fixed or should be reopened; we do not know upstream's stance on that question.

This reproduction used a 0.5B model and a 4-token decode; the interleaved sweep's headline number (7968 vs 0 dispatch hits) is a workload-shape-dependent count, not a universal constant -- it is reported here as a hit-count identity check (0 vs nonzero, reproduced 5/5), not as a claim about hit counts at other prompt lengths or model sizes.

GGML_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=native resolved to '121a-real' for this GB10 GPU; this build has not been tested on any other CUDA architecture, and the buffer-ordering mechanism itself is architecture-independent (it lives in generic backend-scheduling code, not a GPU kernel), so this is noted for completeness, not because architecture is expected to matter.
